newsitem.title: INDIA: Kotak Securities says buy India Hindalco.
newsitem.headline: Kotak Securities says buy India Hindalco.

text.p: Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs, said on Wednesday it put a "buy" recommendation on India's Hindalco Industries in its first ever coverage of the stock.

"Hindalco is our stock of choice in the sector. The stock trades at a justified premium to domestic peers but only in line with international comparables despite having better short-term earnings prospects in the next 12-months," it said in a report.
The securities firm said Hindalco deserved to be traded at a premium relative to its domestic competitors.
Kotak said besides Hindalco's superior trading liquidity, the firm's vertical integration reduced the volatility of its earnings.
"Critically, the company's current programme to expand capacity and raise further the degree of integration gives it considerably higher Earning Per Share growth than its peers."
The securities firm said it expected the aluminium major to show a 4.10 percent fall in 1996/97 (April-March) net profit to 3,848 million.
The firm forecast Hindalco's 1997/98 profit at 5,991 million rupees, up 56 percent in the year-ago period.

It said Hindalco's expansion-cum-modernisation to boost primary metal production by 15 percent to 195,000 tonnes in fiscal 1998 and a further 16 percent to 225,000 tonnes in fiscal 1999 will "synchronise with commodity cycle recovery.'
"Hindalco should benefit from this expansion, which should coincide with expected cycle recovery in aluminium prices."
Initiating its first coverage of India's aluminium industry, Kotak said it had recommended a "moderate overweighting" on the sector.

"This is because the prospect of a reasonable global economic growth in 1997 makes us somewhat more confident of the earnings prospects of India's aluminium producers relative to the prospects of sectors that are purely dependent on India's domestic economy."
